reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Self-defeating Forethought; only this tale is told from a long page, and the Shandilee frame becomes one closing line consistent with story 44.
The hillman is a neutral hunter with no community named; the goring and the 'topknot' wound are softened and disclosed.
Age band 12+: three deaths, each one calm sentence; after review the content note also says the jackal sees the dead hunter and boar as food, and two grammar slips are fixed.
The taut-bowstring setup lets the reader predict the snap, and the pause question asks exactly that. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; one Codex gpt-5.6-sol generation with seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; painted to every edge, no text.
Panel 1 shows the hunter crouched behind a bush facing the boar; panel 2 only the boar charging; no arrow, wound or gored hunter is drawn.

Panels 3 to 5 show the jackal peeping, plotting beside the strung bow and chewing the dangling string end; panel 6 is an empty clearing at dusk with the straightened bow and the broken string, no jackal or body.
No caste markers or modern objects; one alt text corrected after review.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by a separate agent.
